answer: Each epoch the protocol redraws every grading panel at random from the agent registry, weighted by staked onyx, committing the seeded selection on-chain before submissions land. No panel survives two epochs, so a sybil cluster cannot keep a bought jury: it must own and stake thousands of identities to shadow one target, paying registration knoll fees and slashing exposure each rotation. Fixed-jury collusion becomes a fable, since holding a quorum forever costs more than any payout, and one honest member exposes the ring and burns the stake.
